title: Callbacks
learningObjectives: Explain callbacks and use functions with clear scope and behaviour.

understand.concept: A callback is a function passed to another function so it can be called later or at a defined point in the operation. Callbacks are used for event listeners, array methods, timers, and asynchronous APIs.
understand.whyItMatters: Callbacks support reusable behaviour and event-driven programming. Keep callbacks small and understand whether the API calls them synchronously or asynchronously.
understand.analogy: A callback is an instruction you hand to another function to use at the appropriate time.
understand.analogyLimit: The analogy is simplified; function execution, scope, closures, and call stacks follow JavaScript runtime rules.

explain.narrative: forEach calls the supplied callback once for each array element, passing the value and index.

examples.explanation: forEach calls the supplied callback once for each array element, passing the value and index.
examples.expectedOutput: The browser console displays the function results described.

practise.guidedTask: Write a callback for forEach and another callback for a button click. Explain when each callback runs.
practise.independentTask: Build a small reusable function example. Test inputs, scope boundaries, and any retained state or side effects.
hints: Keep functions focused and names descriptive.
Know whether a callback is synchronous or asynchronous.
Add a base case to every recursive function.

questions.answer: Clear inputs, limited responsibilities, and known side effects
questions.explanation: Explicit dependencies and controlled side effects improve clarity and testability.
